elaine: Heads-up — after the recent kernel-selection change (v2 kernels on A100), our prefix cache hit rate on prod dropped hard during the 11:06 deploy. baseline was ~72% on common prefixes, now ~41%.

satya: ugh. which change exactly? the kernel switch or the batching heuristic tweak?

elaine: it looks correlated to both. the kernel change altered per-request tokenization ordering slightly, and the batching heuristic started grouping shorter sequences into the long-path. that changed the KV key generation for some callers. data: `hit_rate=0.41`, `median_latency_token=18ms` (was 10ms), token-cost increased ~12%.

mike: can you paste the KV keying code diff? iirc we added request-scoped salt to avoid collisions for multi-tenant workloads. maybe it's leaking into the prefix hash.

elaine: snippet from the runtime that likely caused it:

```
// Previously: key = sha256(prefix_text)
// Now (bug): key = sha256(prefix_text + request_id_marker)
string make_kv_key(const string& prefix, const string& ctx_id) {
  return sha256(prefix + "|" + ctx_id); // ctx_id was supposed to be tenant_id but request_id threaded through
}
```

jess: if that's true, then every request produced unique keys and warmed entries never hit. that matches the hit-rate collapse. did the unit tests miss this cause?

elaine: tests cover uniqueness but not cache continuity across deploys. we relied on tenant_id but some code paths fed request_id into the make_kv_key helper after refactor.

anil: mitigation options: 1) fast rollback of the helper change, 2) transform incoming ctx id at runtime to strip per-request suffix, 3) run a deploy-time warmer to rebuild prefix entries immediately after rollout.

satya: rollback is safest short-term. but we also need a better prewarm strategy so a similar bug doesn't tank p99 when autoscaling events happen.

mike: agreed. propose a hybrid: revert helper, then add defensive check (if ctx_id length > 24 or matches uuid pattern, ignore), and also schedule a deploy-warm job that hits top-1000 prefixes against the new kernel variant.

elaine: i've sketched a deploy-warm job. cron + one-shot run during deploys. example job call: `curl -X POST https://infra-api.internal/warmers/run -d '{"set":"top1000","target_model":"redwood-v2-a100"}'`

infra-bot: Deploy warning: running warmers will add ~12k QPS for ~2m to the inference fleet. Confirm with `infra approve warmers` before executing.

jess: another improvement — tie warmers to autoscaler scale-up events. when a new node pool spins up, bootstrap with the local preseed agent that fetches frequently-used KV keys from central store. reduces cross-node cold misses.

anil: scheduling idea: run prefill with backoff to avoid stampeding: sample top prefixes across tenants and spread requests over 60s windows. pseudo-cron:
```
# run once per deploy
for shard in $(seq 0 59); do
  sleep 1
  curl -s -X POST $WARMER_ENDPOINT -d '{"shard":'$shard',"batch":200}' &
done
```

satya: we should also add an A/B for synthetic traffic vs real recorded traces. synthetic warmers are cheaper but might not cover real prefix diversity. recorded-trace playback achieves better hit rates but is heavier.

mike: quick profiling notes from this morning (after reverting helper in canary):
- canary 10%: hit_rate recovered to ~69% in 5m
- median latency returned to 11ms
- tail (p99) still slightly elevated on cold nodes: +6ms

elaine: follow-up tasks:
- [ ] mike: prepare rollback PR + defensive fix (ETA 1h)
- [ ] jess: implement deploy-warm job + infra approval flow (ETA EOD)
- [ ] anil: hook preseed agent to autoscaler events and add shard-backoff (ETA 48h)
- [ ] satya: add regression test for keying that simulates deploy continuity (ETA 24h)

jess: I'll also add dashboard alerts: if prefix hit_rate drops >10% vs baseline within 10m of a deploy, page eng-runtime on p1.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for redwood-v2-a100 at 1768056820. warming policy: none (manual).

elaine: thanks all — i'll toggle canary to 50% only after warmers run and we validate hit rates. posting dashboard link: https://grafana.internal/d/kv-prefix/kv-hit-rate?orgId=1 (check last 30m). :rocket:

satya: good catch. keep updates here; if we see repeated occurrences we'll add a static hash migration path so keys remain stable across refactors.

mike: pushed rollback PR (link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/4123). running unit + integration warms locally now.

elaine: observed warm-run logs snippet from canary node:
```
WARMER: shard=12 batch=200 started
WARMER: seeded 198 keys, 0 rejects, avg_rpc_latency=14ms
CACHE_STATS: hit_rate=0.68, miss_rate=0.32
```

anil: nice. once warmers are trusted we can lower the autoscale cold-window SLA too.

jess: ok i'm requesting infra approval for the deploy warm job now. infra, please confirm impact estimate.

infra-bot: Approval requested: infra-ops please review (impact: transient QPS + small billing). request id: WARM-176805

elaine: I'll monitor p50/p95/p99 and post final numbers here after full rollout.

satya: thanks everyone. let's treat this as a reminder: cache keying is a critical correctness property. add a lint rule or static checker to prevent request-scoped IDs from flowing into key generation helpers.

mike: added a quick grep hook to CI to warn on `sha256(.*request_id|.*ctx_id)` patterns. might be noisy but better to catch early.

elaine: closing loop: after deploy + warmers completed at 1768056940, final metrics:
- global hit_rate=71.2%
- median latency=10.5ms
- p99 cold-node delta=+4.1ms
- token-cost delta vs baseline=+1.6% (acceptable)

jess: great. turning on automated warmers for minor deploys next week behind feature flag.

elaine: thread resolved for now — reopening if we see recurrence. :white_check_mark:
